concerns.analysis: The source PDF contains the 'Great Seal of the State of North Carolina' on the first page, which is a meaningful organizational logo identifying the source of the document. The rendered HTML does not contain an element corresponding to this seal.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: The Great Seal of the State of North Carolina on page 1.
concerns.output_quote: Missing element for the state seal in the HTML output.

concerns.analysis: Pages 4 and 5 of the source PDF are infographic-style pages. The text from these pages ('Why Phishing Works', 'A Cautionary Tale in Phishing', 'Ransomware Everywhere') is correctly extracted as HTML text. However, the HTML also includes large images of these graphics that contain the same text, causing the content to be visually duplicated for the user.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Text content on pages 4 and 5 (e.g., 'Why Phishing Works', 'Ransomware Everywhere').
concerns.output_quote: The HTML contains the extracted text for pages 4 and 5, but also embeds large images that include the same text (e.g., alt="A graphic displays text discussing how scammers use desperation..." and alt="An informational graphic with a teal background displays paragraphs of text regarding the rise and dangers of ransomware attacks...").

concerns.description: Output has more images than source PDF (ratio 1.1x) — possible image duplication
concerns.analysis: image_count_ratio=1.10. More images in output than in source indicates duplicated or fabricated image elements.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 7 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=7, examples=['https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/0074-giving-charity', 'https://www.sans.org/security-awareness-training/video-month', 'https://www.sans.org/webcasts/upcoming']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

The source document uses underlining for emphasis in a few locations which is not preserved in the output. For example, on page 1, the text 'You are the target' is underlined (and italicized) in the source, but only italicized in the output. On page 2, the final sentence 'Don't take the bait!' is underlined in the source but lacks any emphasis indicator in the output.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Don't take the bait! (underlined in the PDF)
concerns.location: Page 2, paragraph starting with 'Be sure to check out...'

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (5): 2; 3; SAC the security awareness COMPANY
concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=5. Header/footer elements are present in extraction data. This is common in multi-page government PDFs and is typically cosmetic — the renderer strips them from HTML output.

concerns.description: 2 bare URL(s) in text not converted to hyperlinks: https://www.cisecurity.org/resources/newsletter; https://www.sans.org/security-awareness-training/ouch-newsletter
concerns.analysis: bare_url_count=2. URLs appear as plain text instead of clickable links.
